record.paper_title: Research Problems on Relations Between Nijenhuis Geometry and Integrable Systems
record.original_question: For a candidate integrable PDE system, do its stationary solutions correspond in a natural way to a weakly nonlinear, equivalently linearly degenerate, hydrodynamic-type system?

evidence.quote: TQ3 Do stationary solutions of the system correspond, in a natural sense, to a weakly nonlinear (= linearly degenerate) system of a hydrodynamic type?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a candidate integrable system of partial differential equations for unknown functions $u^1(x,t),\dots,u^n(x,t)$. A stationary solution of $\mathcal{S}$ is a solution with $u^i_t=0$, viewed as a system of ODEs (or, after reduction, as a one-dimensional system) in the spatial variable $x$ together with auxiliary fields obtained from the conserved structure of $\mathcal{S}$. A quasilinear first-order system of hydrodynamic type
$$v^i_t = V^i_j(v)\,v^j_x, \qquad i=1,\dots,N,$$
on functions $v^1(x,t),\dots,v^N(x,t)$ is called weakly nonlinear (equivalently, linearly degenerate) if, in any coordinate system in which the matrix $V^i_j(v)$ has $N$ distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda^1(v),\dots,\lambda^N(v)$ with corresponding right eigenvectors $r_1(v),\dots,r_N(v)$, one has 
$$r_i(\lambda^i) \;=\; \sum_k r_i^k\,\frac{\partial \lambda^i}{\partial v^k} \;=\; 0 \quad \text{for every } i=1,\dots,N,$$
i.e. each characteristic speed is constant along its own characteristic direction.

Question: Determine whether the stationary solutions of $\mathcal{S}$ correspond, in a natural way (e.g., via the standard reduction of the stationary equations of $\mathcal{S}$ to a quasilinear first-order PDE system after introducing appropriate auxiliary variables and a suitable evolution parameter), to a weakly nonlinear (linearly degenerate) hydrodynamic-type system. Formulate this correspondence precisely and either establish it as a general property of integrable systems in the relevant class or exhibit counterexamples.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a general test-question (one of the Bolsinov–Konyaev–Matveev "test questions" for candidate integrable systems) about whether stationary reductions of an integrable PDE system always give rise to weakly nonlinear/linearly degenerate hydrodynamic-type systems. It is formulated as an open guiding problem rather than a theorem, and no general resolution appears in the literature.
